bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Responsible investment / capital-allocation risk as a holding company — BRSR material issue 6. Investment decisions and capital allocation directly influence the long-term financial performance, risk profile and sustainability outcomes of subsidiaries; inadequate consideration of ESG factors may expose the Company to financial, regulatory and reputational risk through underperforming or non-compliant investments, and weak integration could lead to capital misallocation.
- Climate change - physical and transition risk across the subsidiary ecosystem — BRSR material issue 10. Exposure to evolving climate regulations, carbon-related policies, energy and resource cost volatility, physical impacts of extreme weather and rising stakeholder expectations on climate accountability; inadequate management could affect business continuity, asset value and long-term resilience.
- Human rights across subsidiaries and the wider business ecosystem — BRSR material issue 4. As a holding company, exposure extends beyond its own workforce to its subsidiaries; inadequate safeguards on fair labour practices, safe and dignified working conditions, non-discrimination and prevention of harassment could result in regulatory scrutiny, litigation costs, reputational damage and erosion of stakeholder trust.
- Data privacy and cybersecurity — BRSR material issue 7. As digital systems, information flows and data dependencies increase across the Company and its subsidiaries, unauthorised access, data breaches, cyberattacks or failure to comply with data-protection regulation could lead to legal liability, operational disruption and reputational harm.
- Transparent disclosures — BRSR material issue 8. Inadequate, inconsistent or delayed disclosures across the Company or its subsidiaries could expose it to regulatory scrutiny and penalties, reduce stakeholder confidence and impair investors' ability to make informed decisions as governance, ESG and financial reporting requirements keep evolving.
- Circular economy - materials, waste and resource efficiency across investee companies — BRSR material issue 5. Inefficient use of materials, inadequate waste management or limited adoption of circular practices may expose the Company to environmental compliance risk, cost inefficiencies and reputational concerns across its ecosystem of subsidiaries.
- Stakeholder engagement — BRSR material issue 9. Inadequate or inconsistent engagement with employees, shareholders, regulators, subsidiaries and communities may result in misaligned expectations, reputational risk, regulatory challenges and loss of investor confidence.
- Human capital - attrition, skill gaps and leadership continuity — BRSR material issue 3 (its header row is missing from this bundle, which starts mid-word). Weak human capital practices could lead to higher attrition, skill gaps, leadership disruptions and reduced employee engagement.
- Commodity price inflation and availability of labour in the real estate business — Flagged in the MD&A Prospects section as continuing risks even while management expects the overall economic scenario to favour its real estate business.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: KIL holds and manages stakes in Kirloskar Group businesses and owns land, buildings and offices in Pune, Jaipur and Delhi, most of which are given on a leave-and-licence basis to group companies and others; a small residual wind-power business sells generated units to third-party consumers. Its two subsidiaries are Avante Spaces Limited, a Wholly-Owned Subsidiary focused on commercial real estate development at Kothrud, Pune, and Kirloskar Ferrous Industries Limited (45.93% held), a material subsidiary manufacturing pig iron, castings, steel and seamless tubes. The Company operates from a registered and corporate office at One Avante, Kothrud, Pune, with a further office in Mumbai, and serves a single national state with nil exports.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Real estate is the stated core focus area going forward; the Company will pursue development of its own land parcels and new project acquisitions.
- Continue to evaluate opportunities to invest in Group companies and deploy capital to support their investment plans and / or improve the Company's stakes in those companies.
- Through Avante Spaces Limited, develop Avante Business Park Phase-II ('Infinia') at Kothrud, Pune - approximately 1.6 million sq. ft. of Grade A+ commercial office space aimed at multinational corporations, global capability centres, BFSI and technology-driven enterprises.
- Position the Kothrud campus on sustainability and workplace differentiation - ISO 9001/14001/45001 for One Avante, IGBC Platinum, and curated social infrastructure, wellness spaces and a campus-like ecosystem for the new development.
- Invest surplus funds in fixed deposits and mutual funds while deploying part of those funds towards the real estate business.
- At KFIL: customer diversification, export growth and long-term strategic customer relationships across pig iron, castings, steel and tubes; securing new customer approvals is the stated main growth driver in steel and tubes.
- At KFIL: develop new products, reduce operational costs and grow the machining and proto business in castings.
- At KFIL: borrow term loans at competitive rates for capex while reducing overall term and working-capital loans, and hedge USD exposure with forward covers.
- The Company positions itself as a group holding and investment vehicle: it evaluates opportunities to invest in Kirloskar Group companies and to improve its stakes in them, and funds its Wholly-Owned Subsidiary Avante Spaces Limited through inter-corporate loans under Section 186 rather than guarantees - it states it has not granted any guarantee. A Dividend Distribution Policy adopted under SEBI LODR Regulation 43A governs distributions, and a dividend for the year ended 31 March 2026 is put to members as ordinary business at the 32nd AGM. Amounts proposed to be carried to reserves are dealt with as part of the financial performance rather than under a separate reserve policy, and the Company reports no credit ratings obtained during the financial year ('Not applicable'). Foreign exchange earnings and outgo are both reported as Nil, and the Company states there were no material changes or commitments affecting its financial position between the balance-sheet date and the date of the Report.
- The Company has an Environment, Social and Governance Policy that commits it to promoting a circular economy through the reutilisation of resources, thereby reducing waste generation at source.
- Human-rights instruments in place across operations, subsidiaries and strategic investments: Code of Conduct, Human Rights Policy, Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Policy and Whistleblower Policy, with Senior Management and Board oversight, periodic reviews, internal controls and awareness initiatives.
- Climate considerations are integrated into risk management and ESG discussions, with monitoring of regulatory developments and encouragement of energy efficiency and emissions management measures where applicable, under Senior Management and Board oversight.
- Responsible investment principles are being embedded into governance and decision-making, with ESG factors considered alongside financial performance when evaluating and overseeing investments in subsidiaries.
- Engagement with subsidiaries is the stated mechanism for propagating ESG, cybersecurity, disclosure and human-rights standards across the wider business ecosystem, since KIL's own footprint is small.
- NOTE: this bundle contains no quantified or dated ESG target (no emissions, energy, water or diversity goal). The ESG content routed here is the BRSR material-issues risk/opportunity table only.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: This bundle carries no capital-expenditure programme for Kirloskar Industries itself. BRSR Principle 2 reports R&D and capex investments in technologies improving environmental and social impacts as 'NA' for both FY 2026 and FY 2025, with the note that the Company is an unregistered Core Investment Company whose principal business is investing in the group companies, including its Wholly-Owned Subsidiary Avante Spaces Limited, and that Avante and other investee companies are the entities that actually use and invest (the note is cut off mid-sentence). The Board's Report records that the Company continues to invest its surplus funds in fixed deposits and mutual funds and that during the year it deployed part of those funds towards the real estate business. The windmill business - divested earlier on a going-concern basis to ISMT Limited, which was amalgamated with Kirloskar Ferrous Industries Limited effective 8 August 2024 - shall henceforth be operated and managed by KFIL subject to receipt of the requisite statutory approvals and permissions, and remains classified as a discontinuing operation pending completion of those formalities; the Wind Energy Generators generated net wind energy of around 0.94 crores units of electricity in the year against 0.96 crores units previously, and 15,894 RECs were sold with 13,685 unsold RECs held as on 31 March 2026. Headcount rose to 47 employees on the rolls as on 31 March 2026 from 35 previously, including Avante's employees and the Managing and Executive Directors. No plant, line, capacity addition or commissioning timeline for the Company appears anywhere in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The real estate sector is expected to benefit from a benign inflation environment and interest regime, and is likely to continue to strengthen in the quarters ahead.
- Consolidation in the real estate sector is expected to continue, leading to an increase in the market share of corporate and/or organised players such as the Company.
- Commodity price inflation and availability of labour continue to be a risk to the real estate business.
- Management cites India GDP growth moderating to 6.6% in FY 2026-2027 on West Asia conflict headwinds, recovering to 7.2% in FY 2027-2028 assuming energy-market normalisation; global GDP projected at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027.
- India's residential real estate reached a historic H7.3 lakhs crores in housing sales across Tier-1 cities in 2025, contributing around 6% to GDP with long-term potential to expand to ~13% by 2047; demand is concentrated in NCR and other key urban centres and is shifting to a premium-led, higher-ticket market.
- Castings demand was strong across tractor, commercial vehicle, passenger vehicle and engine segments, with production up 17% and increased supplies to key OEM customers.
- Tube sales were driven by robust demand from Automotive, Bearing and Power sectors, improved customer retention and enhanced delivery performance, while the OCTG segment declined on subdued demand from oil exploration companies and high customer inventory.
- Steel pricing remained under pressure from competition from blast furnace - basic oxygen furnace route mills and lower raw material costs.
- Pig iron realisation fell about 6%, from around H 40,600 per MT to around H 38,000 per MT, on margin pressure in the pig iron business; iron ore lump and fines prices stayed firm and blended average coal price ranged USD 170-210 per MT with second-half upward pressure.
- Strategic customer development at KFIL - production expansion plans, transition to in-house engine manufacturing, single-source supplier nominations for new engine platforms and ramp-up of key production programmes - is expected to support future growth.
- KFIL finalised long-term slag sales contracts with cement companies, described as strengthening its strategic market position and providing a stable foundation for future business growth (no quantum or tenor disclosed).
- KFIL cites single source supplier nominations for new engine platforms and ramp up of key production programmes as forward business secured with customers (no quantum disclosed).
